caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 28 of 1989
lawyer:
Asrarul Hossain with Sheikh Abul Hossain and Syeda Afsar Jahan, Advocates ----- For the Defendant-Appellants
Habibul Islam Bhuiyan with Abdul Khaleque, Advocates ----- For the Plaintiff-Respondent.
parties:
Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation Ltd. and others ------ Defendant-Appellants
vs
Abdul Halim Chowdhury ------ Plaintiff-Respondent
full_judgment:
2. The defendants are the appellants before this Court and the plaintiff is the respondent. The respondent being plaintiff instituted the aforesaid suit alleging inter alia that plaintiff was appointed as Assistant Jute Officer of defendant No. 2. Amin Jute Mills Ltd, which is a corporate body under defendant No.1 As Jute Officer of defendant No. 2 the plaintiff purchased 28,178.30 maunds of jute for the season 1982-83 of which he sent 4,444 maunds of jute to UMC Jute Mills, Narshingdi and 23,734.30 maunds of jute to the defendant No. 2 Mill. Thereafter he was posted at Alamnagar Station at Rangpur for the season 1983-84 and during that period a departmental proceeding was started against the plaintiff. During 1982-83 season there was shortage of 471'75 maunds of jute out of purchase by the plaintiff which had been shown as loss to the mill. The plaintiff was also absent for one day i.e. on 22.9.83 without permission of the authority. On the aforesaid allegations charges were framed and issued to the plaintiff. It was the case of the plaintiff that he was illegally dismissed for the aforesaid charges inasmuch as those charges could not be proved against him in accordance with law. 

 5. Mr. Asrarul Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellants, submits that admittedly the plaintiff is an employee of the defendant No. 2, namely, Amin Jute Mills Ltd. Though the Jute Mill was nationalised and placed under the corporation, yet the status of the employees of the Jute Mills remains as master and servant in view of the fact that no rules have been framed for guiding the service conditions of the plaintiff and other employees like the plaintiff. Mr. Asrarul Hossain submits that since the relationship in between defendant No. 2 and the plaintiff still remains as master and servant, the suit in the present form is not maintainable and the relief of the plaintiff is only the suit for damage, if the dismissal order is found, illegal. In this connection Mr. Asrarul Hossain has referred to the case of Md. Motahar Hossain Khan vs. Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation, 36 DLR (AD) 282. He has also referred to the case of Mobarakganj Sugar Mills Ltd. vs. ABM Kazi Nazrul Islam, 1987 BLD (AD) 182. Relying upon those decisions Mr. Asrarul Hossain submits that the present suit is not at all maintainable inasmuch as the relationship between the plaintiff and the defendant No. 2 remains as master and servant and the suit in the present form cannot be entertained. We have gone through the aforesaid decisions of the Appellate Division and it appears to us that the principle laid down by their Lordships of the Appellate Division in above cases are fully applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case and suit for declaration in the present form is not maintainable at all in view of the fact that till now the relationship between plaintiff and the defendant No. 2 is going on as master and servant and though me Corporation had taken over the Jute Mill concerned, namely, the defendant No. 2, no statutory rules have been framed in order to guide the service conditions of the plaintiff and other employees like him. The learned Subordinate Judge has totally failed to consider this aspect of the case. 

 6. Mr. Asrarul Hossain further submits that the plaintiff was an employee of the defendant No. 2 Jute Mills which is controlled and managed by the Jute Mills Corporation. From the record Mr. Asrarul Hossain submits that even the principle of natural justice has been complied with in this case. He submits that charges had been given to the plaintiff and the plaintiff replied to those charges. Thereafter inquiry was held and in that inquiry the plaintiff participated and after considering the matter the inquiry committee found the plaintiff guilty of the charges and recommended for dismissal. So, from the record itself and also from the judgment it clearly appears that the principle of natural justice had been complied with in this case. 

 7. Mr. Asrarul Hossain further submits that in the present case no consequential relief in the form of damages has been prayed for and since no consequential relief has been prayed in the suit, the suit itself is not maintainable as it is hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. In this connection Mr. Asrarul Hossain has referred to the cases of Manager, Personal Division vs. Md. Shazahan Mia 35 DLR, 224 and General Manager, Sonali Bank and others vs. Md. Nurul Hoque Khan 8 BCR, 44. Mr. Asrarul Hossain submits that in these two cases the principle has been laid down that without consequential relief in the form of damages and compensation such a suit cannot be maintained. The learned Advocate further submits that there were appeals against these two decisions before the Appellate Division. But the Appellate Division in preliminary hearing rejected their petitions for special leave to appeal and maintained the judgments passed by the High Court Division. He has filed before us the photo copy of the judgment of the Appellate Division passed in Civil Petition for Special Leave to Appeal No. 299 of 1983 dated 7th February, 1983. In that case the petitioner Shahajahan Miah filed a suit challenging the order of dismissal dated 22.8.73 passed by the Manager, Personal Division, Sonali Bank, Head Office, Dhaka. After considering the matter their Lordships expressed the view that the plaintiffs prayer for declaration was not followed by any consequential relief and, as such, the learned Judges of the High Court Division did not commit any illegality in holding the omission to pray for consequential relief for the purpose of enforcing the declaratory decree was hit by the provisions of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. The learned judges of the High Court Division had given cogent reasons for the decision and there is no reason to interfere with the same and as a result that petition was dismissed. It appears from the plaint as well as from the judgment itself that no consequential relief in the form of compensation and damage has been prayed for So, the decisions as referred to have got full application in the facts and circumstances of the present case. 

 8. Mr. Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, the learned advocate appearing for the plaintiff respondent, submits that the Jute Mills, namely, defendant No. 2, was nationalised and placed under the management and control of the Jute Mills Corporation which is a statutory body. This corporation has got all control and supervision over the jute mills concerned and, as such, the rules and regulations of the Corporation should be followed in the case of the present plaintiff-respondent. It is difficult for us to accept the above contention of Mr. Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, because his above contention has already been answered by their Lordships of the Appellate Division in the aforesaid case reported in 36 DLR (AD) 282. 

 9. We have gone through the judgment passed by the trial Court. It appears to us that the learned Subordinate Judge has gone beyond the jurisdiction to decide the case in view of the fact that the learned Subordinate Judge was not a Court of Appeal over the domestic inquiry made by the Defendant No. 2. The findings as given by the learned trial Court could have been considered if the trial Court was treated as a Court of Appeal under the law. So, the learned Subordinate Judge has totally misconceived the case and, as such, his findings cannot be accepted by us in view of the fact that those were not tenable in the eye of law.
